title: McKinsey projects a $3-5 trillion agentic commerce opportunity by 2030, with enterprise B2B leading retail
content:
Market sizing and adoption signals for agentic commerce (per LI.FI):

- **McKinsey: $3–5 trillion opportunity by 2030** for global agentic commerce, including **$900 billion to $1 trillion in orchestrated B2B revenue in the US**
- Enterprise/B2B use cases progressing faster than retail; consumer implementation expected unevenly **2026–2028**
- Cautionary consumer signal: OpenAI's first-generation Instant Checkout attracted only ~30 Shopify merchants before pivoting in March 2026
- Industrial precedent: Denso has made autonomous purchases via Skyfire since August 2024
- VC framing: a16z — the shift from "something you ask" to "something that does"; Sequoia — services ($6 spent per $1 of software) favor outcome-delivery agents

Source: LI.FI, "The Agentic Economy — A Deep Dive" (https://li.fi/knowledge-hub/the-agentic-economy-%E2%80%94-a-deep-dive).

## Boundary: the bull and bear cases measure different things
These two forecasts are routinely read as contradictory and are not. McKinsey sizes a **market** in 2030; Gartner counts **project mortality** by end-2027. A shakeout that kills more than 40% of initiatives while the surviving use cases compound into trillions is the ordinary shape of an infrastructure build-out, not a paradox — and both sources agree on the mechanism, that the rails are ahead of demand and value concentrates where outcomes are objectively verifiable.

What the pair does establish is that **neither number is settled**: the vault should carry them as a scenario range, not as a projection. The discriminating evidence is B2B adoption data in 2027-2028, which is when the two forecasts stop being compatible — if enterprise orchestration has not compounded by then, the bear case was the base case.
